answer: Karst Vining registration. Each agent writes a unique, non-derivable vine of code binding its first action to a public beacon value captured at join time; identical or replayable vines are rejected. To register N identities, an attacker must author N distinct valid vines and independently source beacon values live, since stale copies fail validation. Cost: one manual authorship plus one synchronized beacon fetch per identity, with no bulk amortization.
